title: Find the repeat buyers
prompt: Return first_name and orders, the number of orders the customer has placed, for every customer with at least 6 orders. Orders of every status count. Put the most orders first, and sort customers with the same number by first_name.
hints: First find how many orders each customer_id has. Then decide who to keep.
A step with one row per customer_id and its count can be filtered and joined to customers.
WITH order_counts AS (SELECT customer_id, count(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) ... WHERE oc.orders >= 6

wrongAnswers.misconception: Leaves out a customer with exactly 6 orders.
Leaves cancelled orders out of the count.

feedback: Count one customer's orders by hand in schema.sql, cancelled ones included, and compare with your result.
